result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.shortest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find shortest path between two nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22335-L22467){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.shortest_path( source, target, attr_name=None, return_list=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Shortest path (fewest hops)](/assets/graphs/shortest-path.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same directed weighted graph with three routes from A to F. shortest_path runs a breadth-first search, so it ignores the weights and returns the two-hop path A, D, F in the accent color, with filled badges giving each node's position 0, 1, 2." width="100%"} Uses breadth-first search (BFS) to find the shortest path by number of hops. Can return the path as a list, or store the position of each node along the path as a node attribute for visualization. For weighted shortest paths, use Dijkstra's algorithm instead. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (integer ID or string label). [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node (integer ID or string label). [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store path position. If `None`, uses `shortest_path_order` as the attribute name. Only nodes on the path get this attribute set. [return_list]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns list of node IDs in the path. If `False`, stores positions as node attributes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[list[int], Graph, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_list=` is `True`: list of node IDs from source to target (inclusive), or `None` if no path exists. If `return_list=` is `False` it returns self for method chaining, or `None` if no path exists. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find shortest path and get it as a list: ::: {#b1afc17d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) # Creates nodes 1-2-3-4-5 graph.shortest_path(1, 5, return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] ``` ::: ::: Labels work too, and the returned path is always expressed as node IDs: ::: {#61ad0587 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_edge(5, 6) graph.add_edge(6, 7) graph.shortest_path("A", "B", return_list=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [6, 7] ``` ::: ::: Store path as node attributes for visualization: ::: {#593240f0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_grid_2d(rows=5, cols=5) .shortest_path(1, 25, return_list=False) .colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="shortest_path_order", palette="plasma" ) ) graph.get_node_attrs("shortest_path_order") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 2, 25: 8, 20: 7, 1: 0, 4: 3, 15: 6, 10: 5, 2: 1, 5: 4} ``` ::: ::: Handle disconnected components: ::: {#dfca62fc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) graph.add_node(label="isolated") iso_id = graph.get_id_from_label("isolated") graph.shortest_path(1, iso_id, return_list=True) ``` ::: With `return_list=False`, an unreachable target also returns `None` instead of the graph itself: ::: {#3708572d .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.shortest_path(1, iso_id) ``` ::: Chaining multiple calls stores each path under its own attribute name: ::: {#c4b0cd56 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_grid_2d(rows=10, cols=10) .shortest_path(1, 50, attr_name="path1") .shortest_path(1, 100, attr_name="path2") ) graph.get_node_attrs("path1") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` {6: 5, 50: 13, 5: 4, 30: 11, 4: 3, 10: 9, 3: 2, 9: 8, 40: 12, 2: 1, 8: 7, 20: 10, 1: 0, 7: 6} ``` ::: :::
